A. The estate of Christ’s exaltation comprehendeth his resurrection, [1] ascension, [2] sitting at the right hand of the Father, [3] and his coming again to judge the world. [4]

A. Christ was exalted in his resurrection, in that, not having seen corruption in death, (of which it was not possible for him to be held,) [5] and having the very same body in which he suffered, with the essential properties thereof, [6] (but without mortality, and other common infirmities belonging to this life,) really united to his soul, [7] he rose again from the dead the third day by his own power; [8] whereby he declared himself to be the Son of God, [9] to have satisfied divine justice, [10] to have vanquished death, and him that had the power of it, [11] and to be Lord of quick and dead: [12] all which he did as a public person, [13] the head of his church, [14] for their justification, [15] quickening in grace, [16] support against enemies, [17] and to assure them of their resurrection from the dead at the last day. [18]

A. Christ was exalted in his ascension, in that having after his resurrection often appeared unto and conversed with his apostles, speaking to them of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God, [19] and giving them commission to preach the gospel to all nations, [20] forty days after his resurrection, he, in our nature, and as our head, [21] triumphing over enemies, [22] visibly went up into the highest heavens, there to receive gifts for men, [23] to raise up our affections thither, [24] and to prepare a place for us, [25] where he himself is, and shall continue till his second coming at the end of the world. [26]

A. Christ is exalted in his sitting at the right hand of God, in that as God-man he is advanced to the highest favour with God the Father, [27] with all fulness of joy, [28] glory, [29] and power over all things in heaven and earth; [30] and does gather and defend his church, and subdue their enemies; furnisheth his ministers and people with gifts and graces, [31] and maketh intercession for them. [32]

A. Christ maketh intercession, by his appearing in our nature continually before the Father in heaven, [33] in the merit of his obedience and sacrifice on earth, [34] declaring his will to have it applied to all believers; [35] answering all accusations against them, [36] and procuring for them quiet of conscience, notwithstanding daily failings, [37] access with boldness to the throne of grace, [38] and acceptance of their persons [39] and services. [40]

A. Christ is to be exalted in his coming again to judge the world, in that he, who was unjustly judged and condemned by wicked men, [41] shall come again at the last day in great power, [42] and in the full manifestation of his own glory, and of his Father’s, with all his holy angels, [43] with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of God, [44] to judge the world in righteousness. [45]

A. Christ, by his mediation, hath procured redemption, [46] with all other benefits of the covenant of grace. [47]

A. We are made partakers of the benefits which Christ hath procured, by the application of them unto us, [48] which is the work especially of God the Holy Ghost. [49]

A. Redemption is certainly applied, and effectually communicated, to all those for whom Christ hath purchased it; [50] who are in time by the Holy Ghost enabled to believe in Christ according to the gospel. [51]

A. They who, having never heard the gospel, [52] know not Jesus Christ, [53] and believe not in him, cannot be saved, [54] be they never so diligent to frame their lives according to the light of nature, [55] or the laws of that religion which they profess; [56] neither is there salvation in any other, but in Christ alone, [57] who is the Savior only of his body the church. [58]

A. All that hear the gospel, and live in the visible church, are not saved; but they only who are true members of the church invisible. [59]

A. The visible church is a society made up of all such as in all ages and places of the world do profess the true religion, [60] and of their children. [61]

A. The visible church hath the privilege of being under God’s special care and government; [62] of being protected and preserved in all ages, notwithstanding the opposition of all enemies; [63] and of enjoying the communion of saints, the ordinary means of salvation, [64] and offers of grace by Christ to all the members of it in the ministry of the gospel, testifying, that whosoever believes in him shall be saved, [65] and excluding none that will come unto him. [66]

A. The invisible church is the whole number of the elect, that have been, are, or shall be gathered into one under Christ the head. [67]

A. The members of the invisible church by Christ enjoy union and communion with him in grace and glory. [68]

A. The union which the elect have with Christ is the work of God’s grace, [69] whereby they are spiritually and mystically, yet really and inseparably, joined to Christ as their head and husband; [70] which is done in their effectual calling. [71]

A. Effectual calling is the work of God’s almighty power and grace, [72] whereby (out of his free and special love to his elect, and from nothing in them moving him thereunto) [73] he doth, in his accepted time, invite and draw them to Jesus Christ, by his Word and Spirit; [74] savingly enlightening their minds, [75] renewing and powerfully determining their wills, [76] so as they (although in themselves dead in sin) are hereby made willing and able freely to answer his call, and to accept and embrace the grace offered and conveyed therein. [77]

A. All the elect, and they only, are effectually called: [78] although others may be, and often are, outwardly called by the ministry of the Word, [79] and have some common operations of the Spirit; [80] who, for their wilful neglect and contempt of the grace offered to them, being justly left in their unbelief, do never truly come to Jesus Christ. [81]

A. The communion in grace which the members of the invisible church have with Christ, is their partaking of the virtue of his mediation, in their justification, [82] adoption, [83] sanctification, and whatever else, in this life, manifests their union with him. [84]

A. Justification is an act of God’s free grace unto sinners, [85] in which he pardoneth all their sins, accepteth and accounteth their persons righteous in his sight; [86] not for any thing wrought in them, or done by them, [87] but only for the perfect obedience and full satisfaction of Christ, by God imputed to them, [88] and received by faith alone. [89]

A. Although Christ, by his obedience and death, did make a proper, real, and full satisfaction to God’s justice in the behalf of them that are justified; [90] yet in as much as God accepteth the satisfaction from a surety, which he might have demanded of them, and did provide this surety, his own only Son, [91] imputing his righteousness to them, [92] and requiring nothing of them for their justification but faith, [93] which also is his gift, [94] their justification is to them of free grace. [95]

A. Justifying faith is a saving grace, [96] wrought in the heart of a sinner by the Spirit [97] and Word of God, [98] whereby he, being convinced of his sin and misery, and of the disability in himself and all other creatures to recover him out of his lost condition, [99] not only assenteth to the truth of the promise of the gospel, [100] but receiveth and resteth upon Christ and his righteousness, therein held forth, for pardon of sin, [101] and for the accepting and accounting of his person righteous in the sight of God for salvation. [102]

A. Faith justifies a sinner in the sight of God, not because of those other graces which do always accompany it, or of good works that are the fruits of it, [103] nor as if the grace of faith, or any act thereof, were imputed to him for his justification; [104] but only as it is an instrument by which he receiveth and applieth Christ and his righteousness. [105]

A. Adoption is an act of the free grace of God, [106] in and for his only Son Jesus Christ, [107] whereby all those that are justified are received into the number of his children, [108] have his name put upon them, [109] the Spirit of his Son given to them, [110] are under his fatherly care and dispensations, [111] admitted to all the liberties and privileges of the sons of God, made heirs of all the promises, and fellow-heirs with Christ in glory. [112]

A. Sanctification is a work of God’s grace, whereby they whom God hath, before the foundation of the world, chosen to be holy, are in time, through the powerful operation of his Spirit [113] applying the death and resurrection of Christ unto them, [114] renewed in their whole man after the image of God; [115] having the seeds of repentance unto life, and all other saving graces, put into their hearts, [116] and those graces so stirred up, increased, and strengthened, [117] as that they more and more die unto sin, and rise unto newness of life. [118]

A. Repentance unto life is a saving grace, [119] wrought in the heart of a sinner by the Spirit [120] and Word of God, [121] whereby, out of the sight and sense, not only of the danger, [122] but also of the filthiness and odiousness of his sins, [123] and upon the apprehension of God’s mercy in Christ to such as are penitent, [124] he so grieves for [125] and hates his sins, [126] as that he turns from them all to God, [127] purposing and endeavouring constantly to walk with him in all the ways of new obedience. [128]

A. Although sanctification be inseparably joined with justification, [129] yet they differ, in that God in justification imputeth the righteousness of Christ; [130] in sanctification of his Spirit infuseth grace, and enableth to the exercise thereof; [131] in the former, sin is pardoned; [132] in the other, it is subdued: [133] the one doth equally free all believers from the revenging wrath of God, and that perfectly in this life, that they never fall into condemnation [134] the other is neither equal in all, [135] nor in this life perfect in any, [136] but growing up to perfection. [137]

A. The imperfection of sanctification in believers ariseth from the remnants of sin abiding in every part of them, and the perpetual lustings of the flesh against the spirit; whereby they are often foiled with temptations, and fall into many sins, [138] are hindered in all their spiritual services, [139] and their best works are imperfect and defiled in the sight of God. [140]

A. True believers, by reason of the unchangeable love of God, [141] and his decree and covenant to give them perseverance, [142] their inseparable union with Christ, [143] his continual intercession for them, [144] and the Spirit and seed of God abiding in them, [145] can neither totally nor finally fall away from the state of grace, [146] but are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation. [147]

A. Such as truly believe in Christ, and endeavour to walk in all good conscience before him, [148] may, without extraordinary revelation, by faith grounded upon the truth of God’s promises, and by the Spirit enabling them to discern in themselves those graces to which the promises of life are made, [149] and bearing witness with their spirits that they are the children of God, [150] be infallibly assured that they are in the estate of grace, and shall persevere therein unto salvation. [151]

A. Assurance of grace and salvation not being of the essence of faith, [152] true believers may wait long before they obtain it; [153] and, after the enjoyment thereof, may have it weakened and intermitted, through manifold distempers, sins, temptations, and desertions; [154] yet they are never left without such a presence and support of the Spirit of God as keeps them from sinking into utter despair. [155]

A. The communion in glory which the members of the invisible church have with Christ, is in this life, [156] immediately after death, [157] and at last perfected at the resurrection and day of judgment. [158]

A. The members of the invisible church have communicated to them in this life the firstfruits of glory with Christ, as they are members of him their head, and so in him are interested in that glory which he is fully possessed of; [159] and, as an earnest thereof, enjoy the sense of God’s love, [160] peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Ghost, and hope of glory; [161] as, on the contrary, sense of God’s revenging wrath, horror of conscience, and a fearful expectation of judgment, are to the wicked the beginning of their torments which they shall endure after death. [162]

A. Death being threatened as the wages of sin, [163] it is appointed unto all men once to die; [164] for that all have sinned. [165]

A. The righteous shall be delivered from death itself at the last day, and even in death are delivered from the sting and curse of it; [166] so that, although they die, yet it is out of God’s love, [167] to free them perfectly from sin and misery, [168] and to make them capable of further communion with Christ in glory, which they then enter upon. [169]

A. The communion in glory with Christ, which the members of the invisible church enjoy immediately after death is, in that their souls are then made perfect in holiness, [170] and received into the highest heavens, [171] where they behold the face of God in light and glory, [172] waiting for the full redemption of their bodies, [173] which even in death continue united to Christ, [174] and rest in their graves as in their beds, [175] till at the last day they be again united to their souls. [176] Whereas the souls of the wicked are at their death cast into hell, where they remain in torments and utter darkness, and their bodies kept in their graves, as in their prisons, till the resurrection and judgment of the great day. [177]

A. We are to believe that at the last day there shall be a general resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust: [178] when they that are then found alive shall in a moment be changed; and the selfsame bodies of the dead which were laid in the grave, being then again united to their souls forever, shall be raised up by the power of Christ. [179] The bodies of the just, by the Spirit of Christ, and by virtue of his resurrection as their head, shall be raised in power, spiritual, incorruptible, and made like to his glorious body; [180] and the bodies of the wicked shall be raised up in dishonour by him, as an offended judge. [181]

A. Immediately after the resurrection shall follow the general and final judgment of angels and men; [182] the day and hour whereof no man knoweth, that all may watch and pray, and be ever ready for the coming of the Lord. [183]

A. At the day of judgment, the wicked shall be set on Christ’s left hand, [184] and, upon clear evidence, and full conviction of their own consciences, [185] shall have the fearful but just sentence of condemnation pronounced against them; [186] and thereupon shall be cast out from the favourable presence of God, and the glorious fellowship with Christ, his saints, and all his holy angels, into hell, to be punished with unspeakable torments, both of body and soul, with the devil and his angels forever. [187]

A. At the day of judgment, the righteous, being caught up to Christ in the clouds, [188] shall be set on his right hand, and there openly acknowledged and acquitted, [189] shall join with him in the judging of reprobate angels and men, [190] and shall be received into heaven, [191] where they shall be fully and forever freed from all sin and misery; [192] filled with inconceivable joys, [193] made perfectly holy and happy both in body and soul, in the company of innumerable saints and holy angels, [194] but especially in the immediate vision and fruition of God the Father, of our Lord Jesus Christ, and of the Holy Spirit, to all eternity. [195] And this is the perfect and full communion, which the members of the invisible church shall enjoy with Christ in glory, at the resurrection and day of judgment.
